title: Burnham’s first budget should take a global approach to deliver for the UK
gist: Chatham House argues the first Burnham budget must treat geoeconomics as a fiscal variable: UK gas-linked power prices, food and fertiliser exposure, and gilt yields at 6% make domestic tax-and-spend insufficient, and it proposes five measures to measure and cut exposure.

themes.theme: Energy and food cost of living

insights.claim: UK electricity prices are set mainly by gas prices, leaving the UK more vulnerable to global price spikes than many comparable countries; Ofgem raised the price cap about £60 to £1,723 in October as the Iran war lifted wholesale gas.
insights.so_what: UK inflation and consumer sentiment remain tied to gas; watch the January cap reset.
insights.locator: Cost of living: energy and food
insights.speaker: Chatham House

insights.claim: Analysts forecast a further 16 per cent rise in UK energy bills from January.
insights.so_what: Adds to near-term UK inflation pressure and the case for rates staying higher.
insights.locator: Cost of living: energy and food
insights.speaker: Chatham House

insights.claim: The Food and Drink Federation expects UK food inflation to pass 6 per cent by mid-2027, citing energy costs from the Middle East conflict, drought and El Niño, with gas-based fertiliser adding pressure.
insights.so_what: Food inflation is under-discussed relative to energy and shapes household inflation perceptions.
insights.locator: Cost of living: energy and food
insights.speaker: Chatham House

insights.claim: Food and energy spikes shape household inflation perceptions and can keep interest rates higher for longer, per Bank of England research.
insights.so_what: Supports a higher-for-longer UK rate path when commodity shocks persist.
insights.locator: Cost of living: energy and food
insights.speaker: Chatham House

insights.claim: A global bond sell-off pushed the 30-year gilt yield briefly above 6 per cent this month and ate into the chancellor's fiscal headroom, which may shrink further.
insights.so_what: Gilt term premium and thin headroom make the budget a volatility event for UK duration and sterling.
insights.locator: Growth and jobs: capital and barriers
insights.speaker: Chatham House

insights.claim: The chain from the Iran war runs through costlier energy and food to higher inflation, higher rates and a higher cost of capital that growth depends on.
insights.so_what: Geopolitical energy shocks transmit to UK fiscal space through rates.
insights.speaker: Chatham House

insights.claim: The Treasury and the Office for Budget Responsibility treat global forces as background sensitivities to the forecast, an approach that worked when markets were calm and allies reliable but fails now.
insights.so_what: Official forecasts may understate global-shock sensitivity.
insights.speaker: Chatham House

insights.claim: The budget should publish a statement of UK sensitivity to global borrowing costs, gas prices and food import prices, with measurable targets to cut it over this parliament.
insights.so_what: A published exposure yardstick would be a new fiscal-credibility signal to watch.
insights.speaker: Chatham House

insights.claim: To cut gas dependence the budget should move the remaining quarter of the Renewables Obligation cost to general taxation, bring forward the £15 billion Warm Homes Plan, and secure gas storage, all classed as risk-reducing investment within the capital budget and co-financed by the National Wealth Fund.
insights.so_what: Shifting levies off electricity bills would favor electrification over gas.
insights.locator: 2. Cut energy bills by reducing gas dependence
insights.speaker: Chatham House

insights.claim: Britain holds around 12 days of gas storage compared with 89 in Germany by one estimate, and its largest site, Rough, could close next spring without a deal.
insights.so_what: UK winter gas price spikes are structurally likelier; Rough's fate is a watch item.
insights.locator: 2. Cut energy bills by reducing gas dependence
insights.speaker: Chatham House

insights.claim: Britain's last large ammonia plant at Billingham closed in 2023 because UK gas prices made it uncompetitive, so fertiliser is now made from imported ammonia at global prices.
insights.so_what: UK farm inputs are directly exposed to global gas and ammonia prices.
insights.locator: 3. Protect food supply against the next fertiliser shock
insights.speaker: Chatham House

insights.claim: The paper proposes a strategic fertiliser reserve and National Wealth Fund support for low-carbon ammonia linked to UK hydrogen projects.
insights.so_what: Possible policy tailwind for UK hydrogen and ammonia projects.
insights.locator: 3. Protect food supply against the next fertiliser shock
insights.speaker: Chatham House

insights.claim: It proposes scaling the £50 million critical minerals fund into a stockpile, expanding UK Export Finance guarantees to diversify mineral supply, and a UK carbon border levy exempting comparable carbon-pricing partners starting with the EU.
insights.so_what: Signals UK alignment with EU carbon-pricing architecture and minerals stockpiling.
insights.speaker: Chatham House

insights.claim: The chancellor has deferred a path to higher defence spending to next year's spending review, and setting out that trajectory and its funding would remove a major source of investor uncertainty.
insights.so_what: UK defence budget path is an unresolved upside risk to gilt supply and to defence equities.
insights.locator: 5. Treat UK credibility as an asset
insights.speaker: Chatham House

insights.claim: The UK-EU summit on 20 November is a chance to link emissions trading systems, Canada's proposed Defence, Security and Resilience Bank offers a way to share defence costs, and the UK's upcoming G20 presidency can advance shared energy, food, fertiliser and sovereign debt resilience.
insights.so_what: ETS linkage on 20 November is a dated UK-EU catalyst.
insights.speaker: Chatham House

insights.claim: The US has embraced tariffs, the EU is strengthening trade defence tools, and China is leveraging rare earths while pushing exports aggressively, each changing the terms on which UK firms invest, trade and hire.
insights.so_what: UK is a price taker among protectionist blocs.
insights.locator: Growth and jobs: capital and barriers
insights.speaker: Chatham House
